transcript.text: We replaced our old condenser dryer with a heat pump one about a month ago and honestly it's driving me mad, a normal load of towels takes nearly 3 and a half hours, the old one did it in about 90 minutes. It also feels barely warm for the first half hour when I open the door to check. Surely that's not right? Is it faulty?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. It is not necessarily faulty, as heat pump dryers are significantly slower than condenser models and typically take longer to dry heavy items like towels. The "barely warm" feeling in the first half hour is normal for this technology as it slowly builds up heat efficiency over time. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Heat-pump dryers dry at a lower temperature and take noticeably longer than vented or condenser dryers; clothes come out warm rather than hot. It would be worth a closer look if clothes are still wet at the end of a full cycle with clean filters and an emptied water tank. Damp laundry is most often an airflow problem, and the first free check is the fluff filter in the door opening — heat-pump models often have a second filter at the bottom too. Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), is the mesh torn, or was it already clean?

Well I clean the fluff filter after every single load, so that's not the problem. I cleaned the other filter at the bottom about two weeks ago and it looked clean. The clothes do come out dry in the end, it just takes forever!
Is it genuinely cold and never drying, or does it dry but just feels cooler / slower than your old dryer?
It does dry, the clothes are fully dry at the end, it just takes ages. It's only lukewarm at the start, not cold. Is that normal?

Yes, it is normal for a heat pump tumble dryer to take significantly longer than an old condenser model. Heat pumps are designed to be energy efficient by using lower temperatures, which results in longer drying times but still achieves dry clothes. Behind the flap at the bottom front there's a condenser unit (or a second filter on heat-pump models). Take it out and rinse the fluff off under the tap, then let it drip-dry and refit it. Was it clogged with fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

I already told you, I rinsed that one two weeks ago and it looked clean. Do you think it's the garage being cold? It's only about 8-10 degrees out there at the moment, and I keep opening the door to check on it too.

Yes, a garage temperature of 8-10°C can significantly increase drying times for heat pump tumble dryers. These appliances rely on extracting heat from the surrounding air, so colder environments reduce their efficiency and extend cycle durations. From what you have described, the most likely cause is check load size, load wetness and programme. Some programmes (cool air, refresh, delicates or a low-heat option) dry with little or no heat. Was a cool-air or low-heat programme set (and have you changed it), or was it a normal heat programme?
I've been using Cotton Cupboard Dry with a full load, so that's a normal heat programme, nothing like cool air or low heat. Should I be doing something different?

Yes, you should stop opening the door during the cycle as this releases heat and significantly extends drying times. Ensure you are not overloading the machine, as a full load of towels requires more space for air circulation to dry efficiently. Overloading, or putting clothes in that weren't spun well in the washer, makes drying much slower. The drum should be no more than about two-thirds full. Was it overloaded or were the clothes very wet going in (and have you changed that), or was it a normal, well-spun load?
It's a full load of towels, so yes quite full I suppose, but they're spun at 1000 rpm in the washer. I do open the door two or three times to check on it. Is that what's making it so slow?

Yes, opening the door frequently allows heat to escape and resets the drying cycle, which significantly increases drying time. Additionally, running a full load of towels on a Cotton Cupboard Dry programme in a cold garage will naturally take much longer than your previous machine did. Run a normal heat programme again for 10–15 minutes. Is it heating now, or still cold?
It's not cold, it's just lukewarm like I said at the start. Even after an hour it's only warm when I open the door, not scorching like the old one. Is that how it should be?
No, a heat pump dryer taking 3. 5 hours for towels in a cold garage is not normal performance. Run a normal drying programme with a normal load. Is the laundry coming out dry now, or still damp?
The clothes do come out fully dry at the end, like I said, it's just the time it takes. So what should I actually do, is it faulty or not?

It does not appear to be faulty, as the clothes are drying completely. Heat pump dryers operate at lower temperatures and take significantly longer than condenser models, especially in a cold garage. Check the vent hose out of the back: it should be short, without kinks or squashed sections, and clear of fluff all the way to the outside vent. Was it kinked, squashed or blocked (and is it sorted), or was it already clear?
